- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.
- If model forecast mean is significantly below true outcome mean (e.g., >1.5% gap), consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with recent trend strength.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > -0.05), model often underestimates upward momentum — raise forecast by 0.3–0.8% to capture sentiment-driven rally.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility — add 0.2–0.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or recent price action is erratic.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope and reduce peak magnitude by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
